response:
It makes a lot of sense that dissociation once protected you—and it's a real sign of growth that you can recognize when it's no longer serving you.

A helpful first step is grounding yourself in the present moment when you notice you're drifting. Try engaging your senses: name five things you can see, hold something cold or textured, press your feet firmly into the floor, or focus on slow breathing. Some people find it useful to keep an anchor object nearby or to say the date and where they are out loud. Noticing your early warning signs—like feeling foggy or distant—can also give you a chance to intervene sooner.

That said, dissociation is often tied to past trauma, and working through it usually goes deeper than self-help alone. A trauma-informed therapist can help you build tools tailored to you and address the underlying causes safely. You've already shown insight and strength here—that's a meaningful start.
